title: actor.register — Response
description: 201 Created on first call: returns BOTH `actor` and `token` for the newly registered human or agent actor. The plaintext `token` is shown exactly once. On idempotent replay (same operation_id + same request_hash) the response MUST OMIT the `token` field and return only `actor`; replay preserves the token-redaction exception and MUST NOT reissue the plaintext token. There is intentionally no token-recovery path: if a human token is lost, an authenticated holder of an active human credential MUST call actor.revoke_token and then actor.register a fresh human actor. If an agent-session token is lost, the responsible active human MUST call actor.deactivate and then actor.register a fresh agent session. `token` is therefore not in `required`; conformant implementations enforce its presence on first call and its absence on replay via the paired registration fixtures.

actor.description: Canonical actor envelope for the newly registered actor. Human registrations return the existing human shape. Agent registrations MUST return an agent actor with runtime and parent linkage populated.

kind.description: Human registration responses return a human actor.

agent_runtime.description: Humans do not have an agent runtime.

parent_actor_id.description: Humans do not have a parent actor linkage.

kind.description: Agent registration responses return an agent actor.

agent_runtime.description: Runtime identifier for the registered agent session.

parent_actor_id.description: Human actor responsible for spawning the registered agent session.

token.description: Opaque bearer credential. Returned ONLY on the first call for a given operation_id. Implementations MUST NOT return this field on idempotent replay. Implementations MUST NOT log or store this value in plaintext after returning it.
